name: contact
description: An identity card that encodes a vCard: name, title and contact lines beside a QR that saves the presenter to a phone.
purpose: Use as the "scan to add me" close or a speaker-intro slide. The QR encodes a vCard the audience saves in one tap, or, with `qr: tel`, a link that dials; the card shows the name as hero with title/org and a contact ledger. Author the fields as a postfix-key list. It reflows by canvas (side by side, then stacked) and holds at every venue.

title.description: Optional framing heading; the person's name is the visual hero, drawn from the `name` field.

fields.description: One field per bullet in postfix-key form — value first, trailing inline-code names the field: `- Sharmarke Aden `name``. Keys: name (required), title|role, org|company, email, phone|tel|voice, mobile|cell, office|work, url|web|site. Phone keys are separate lines, each typed in the vCard, and the ledger lists every line in the order you wrote it. Optional keys: `caption` (CTA under the QR) and `qr` (what the code carries: `vcard`, `tel` or `url`).

caption.description: Optional call-to-action under the QR, as a postfix-key bullet: ``- Scan to add me `caption` ``.

skeleton:
<!-- _class: contact -->

## Add me.

- Full Name `name`
- Title `title`
- Organization `org`
- name@example.com `email`
- Scan to add me `caption`
sample:
<!-- _class: contact -->

- Ada Slide `name`
- One scan saves the speaker `title`
- Laticent `org`
- hello@laticent.io `email`
- laticent.io `url`
- The QR encodes this card as a vCard `caption`

whenToUse.title: The scan-to-add-me close
whenToUse.body: End a pitch or intro with a code the audience scans to save your contact, instead of trading business cards.

whenToUse.title: Show what you choose, encode the rest
whenToUse.body: Every non-empty field goes into the vCard; the card foregrounds the name, title and org and lists email/phone/url beneath.

whenToUse.title: A hall or conference room
whenToUse.body: A full vCard is a dense code (55-67 modules wide) and the back row cannot resolve it. Add `- tel `qr`` or `- url `qr``: the code carries only a phone link or a web address (27-35 modules, about 2.5 times larger per module) and the ledger still shows every field.

whenToUse.title: Phone numbers that differ
whenToUse.body: Write each line with its own key (`mobile`, `office`, `phone`). Each becomes its own typed TEL entry in the vCard, and the card lists them in the order written.

antiPatterns.title: Not a team roster
antiPatterns.body: One card is one person. For a set of people use an inventory layout; a contact card is a single identity.

antiPatterns.title: Don't bold the field values
antiPatterns.body: The value leads and the key trails as a small tag — name last, never first. Writing the key first, bolded, breaks the transform's postfix read.

related.name: wifi
related.when: the card is a network to join rather than a person

commonMistakes.mistake: No field is tagged with the `name` key.
commonMistakes.fix: Every contact card needs exactly one field trailing `` `name` `` — without it the vCard has no identity and the hero name area renders empty.

commonMistakes.mistake: The trailing key doesn't match a supported alias, e.g. `` `position` `` instead of `` `title`/`role` ``.
commonMistakes.fix: Only the documented keys are recognized (name, title|role, org|company, email, phone|tel|voice, mobile|cell, office|work, url|web|site, qr, caption) — an unrecognized key isn't mapped to any card field, so the whole bullet is silently dropped from both the rendered card and the vCard, not merely misplaced.

commonMistakes.mistake: A full vCard QR on a `venue: hall` deck.
commonMistakes.fix: The code is dense and the room is far. Add `- tel `qr`` (the code dials the first phone line) or `- url `qr``; the card still lists everything.

venueCapacity.none: A fixed card, so there is no count budget. `npm run check:venue-conformance` checks its fit at every venue and canvas instead.
